title: PET EXORCISM AT ZAGREB PARK: Priest casts Satan out of a Maltese and bloodthirsty hamsters

content:
Every day brings more crime section stories in the Croatian media about pets out of control. Attacks by aggressive dogs, uncontrolled emptying of cat bladders into potted houseplants, toothy hamsters and rabbits chewing cables and furniture, and giant parrots screaming Tito-party-youth-action prompted an association of victims of impossible pets—"Friends of Humans"—to organize a mass exorcism in cooperation with the City of Zagreb and the Archdiocese of Zagreb.

Oglas

"Honestly, I can't wash the dog semen out of my pants from everything my Ringo unloads when he humps my leg. And the fifteen or so times he licks his own genitals and testicles, which I witness every day, has become too much for my stomach. That's why I came here so that with Christ's help we can resolve these acts of fornication by my dog," explains Veselko, the owner of a German Shepherd whose unsheathed member swung the entire time because of all the females nearby.

The archdiocese's exorcist approached each dog, for example, and tested whether Satan was in it by offering a treat and telling it: "Pray! Come on! Pray!" Dogs that did not stand on their hind legs and fold their front paws in a pose of humble prayer were clearly servants of the Evil One and spawn of his guard dog Cerberus. For them came a muzzle, incense, dunking in holy water, and an electric shock collar shaped like a crucifix, all until the dog was broken and brought to a state of humility.

"There wasn't even a test for my cat. The priest says cats are deceitful and can't be trusted, so he performed an exorcism immediately as a precaution. My John broke down the moment they dipped him in holy water. He hates water, and holy water apparently even more," a Siamese cat owner explained of the feline treatment.

The biggest problem at this mass exorcism was caused by a 35-year-old red macaw named Paul, who would not stop chanting "religion is the opium of the people," "death to fascism," "the window must fall tonight—Tito," and similar anti-Catholic slogans. In the end, the priest was forced to pluck all that communist plumage, after which the bird fell silent.

Oglas

"I'm glad it's all over now. That bird has been causing me problems since 1991. I explained to him that this is Croatia now, that Yugoslavia is gone, that I'm not a distinguished member of the Communist Party but an esteemed member of the HDZ, and to stop embarrassing me in front of people by calling me 'Comrade Milić,'" Mr. Milić recounted with visible relief after the exorcism of his bird.

The entire ceremony went smoothly with only one minor incident. One dog, Đorđe, reacted very poorly to the whole ritual, so the priest asked the owner what breed it was. When he learned it was a "Serbian Tricolour Hound," he was forced to put the dog down because it was a Serb and Eastern Orthodox.
